name: Masculism
summary: Masculism is a loosely defined current that treats men as a sex facing systematic disadvantages, in areas such as conscription, custody, suicide, health and schooling, and rejects the claim that men as a group hold power over women. Its mainstream, represented by Warren Farrell, wants gender liberation for both sexes, but writers also use the term for antifeminism or the promotion of masculine ideals.
scope: The progressive or egalitarian masculist strand of Warren Farrell, Ferrel Christensen and the men's movement, as described on Wikipedia and in Farrell's own writing. It excludes the male-supremacist 'extremist' strand and the Christian Mighty Men movements, which differ on gender roles. Masculism has no doctrine outside gender, family and conscription issues, so most answers on other topics are neutral and low-confidence.

sources.title: Warren Farrell
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Farrell's trajectory and claims on conscription, suicide, domestic violence, pay gap and affirmative action.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Farrell cites men's shorter life spans and health neglect, but no masculist source states a view on universal healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage floors are not a masculist issue and adherents range across economic views.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Economic organisation is outside masculism; Farrell's pay analysis uses market choices but does not defend markets generally.

public-ownership.rationale: Ownership of utilities is not addressed by any masculist source.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Tax levels on the rich are outside masculism's gender focus.

unions-good.rationale: Farrell stresses that men fill the most dangerous jobs and most workplace deaths, but neither he nor the masculism literature says whether unions help; no answer can be drawn from that.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights are not discussed in masculist sources, though divorce asset division concerns men.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Masculist writing targets courts, the draft and health spending, not business regulation, and adherents run from libertarian to left on economics.

cut-welfare.rationale: Farrell criticises the expectation that men earn and provide, but no masculist source takes a side on cutting welfare programmes as such.

worker-ownership.rationale: Masculist sources discuss men's paid work only as a burden of the provider role; collective ownership of firms is never raised.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Counter-terrorism surveillance is not a masculist concern and adherents hold varied civil-liberties views.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Drug policy is outside masculism, which has no stated position on adult drug use.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Masculists complain about 'man bashing' in institutions, but they would be wary of speech laws; inferred only weakly.

strong-leader.rationale: Masculism has no view on leadership structure, though the mythopoetic strand valorises masculine leadership figures.

state-harmful.rationale: Masculists want state reform of family law and courts rather than abolishing the state, so they would disagree; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: No documented masculist stance on funding; the concern is who bears risk, and Farrell's critique concerns men being sent to die, not budgets.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed by masculist sources; adherents divide between moral conservatives and libertarian-leaning members.

decide-locally.rationale: Local versus national decision-making is not addressed, though masculists ask for uniform family law standards.

rehabilitation.rationale: Masculists object to sentencing disparities for men but have no stated view on prison purpose.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents split between the mythopoetic and Christian masculinist strands that favour traditional families and the progressive strand that wants flexible roles.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Masculism as a gender movement takes no position, and its strands range from progressive to religiously conservative.

abortion-legal.rationale: Masculism raises men's lack of say over fatherhood but has no settled position on whether abortion should be legal.

more-religion-public.rationale: Christian masculinist groups such as Mighty Men want more religion in public life while the progressive strand is secular, so no common view.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Masculists oppose preferences by sex and Farrell doubts affirmative action, but active correction of racial injustice is not addressed directly.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Farrell stresses socialisation into rigid roles (men as success objects), but also treats some sex differences as real, and the traditionalist strand grounds roles in nature.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Masculism is not tied to nationalism; the question is outside its scope.

gradual-change.rationale: Masculism has no stated view on the pace of social change, though its critics of feminism may favour reversing some recent reforms.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration levels never come up in Farrell's work or the Wikipedia overview of masculism, whose issues are custody, conscription, violence and health.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Masculism takes no stance on the UN or similar bodies; the movement is mostly national in its legal targets.

free-trade.rationale: The masculist agenda of custody, draft and health reform says nothing about trade, so no position can be read off it.

nation-first.rationale: Farrell's foreign-policy remarks are limited to who is drafted and who dies in combat; the trade-off between national interest and global cooperation is not discussed.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; Farrell's concern is who is sent to fight, not whether to intervene.

open-borders.rationale: No masculist text addresses border policy; the movement's grievances concern family courts and male-only obligations within a country.

limit-growth.rationale: Farrell compares neglect of men's health to ignoring global warming, but only as an analogy; masculists take no view on limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate appears in Farrell only as a metaphor for interconnection between the sexes, which gives no basis for a policy answer.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss technological optimism; their arguments are about social roles and law, not technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy, including nuclear power, is absent from Farrell's writing and from accounts of masculism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Masculist aims are pursued through advocacy and law reform, so revolution is inferred to be rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Masculists distrust academic experts in gender studies, but there is no general stance on expert rule.

central-planning.rationale: Masculist sources do not compare planned and market economies; adherents are found on both left and right.

socialized-markets.rationale: Who should own businesses is not a question the masculism literature raises, so no answer is attributed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design, including land taxation, is not discussed by Farrell or other masculist authors.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Masculists talk about money mainly through alimony, child support and men's earning pressure; inheritance tax is not discussed.

basic-income.rationale: Farrell questions men's duty to be the breadwinner, which might bear on income support, but no source mentions basic income, so this stays neutral.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protecting domestic industry is not part of the masculist programme of custody, conscription and men's health reform.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial strategy never appears in masculist sources; no stance can be attributed.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist ideas about property ownership are absent from masculist writing.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Farrell discusses pay as a trade-off that people choose, not something to abolish.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Monetary policy lies wholly outside masculism, whose sources say nothing on central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Masculist authors do not discuss wage-setting institutions or corporatism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Nothing supports one-party rule; masculists rely on public advocacy and courts, inferred.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Not addressed; masculism is not tied to a constitutional form.

democracy-best.rationale: Masculist movements work through democratic advocacy, but no source states a ranking of regimes.

direct-votes.rationale: How laws are made, by referendum or representatives, is not discussed in masculist sources, which lobby existing legislatures and courts.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-based government is foreign to the masculism literature, which works through existing democratic institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: No masculist source addresses regional secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: The progressive strand rejects male superiority, though the extremist male-supremacist strand would say some are naturally suited; mainstream inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: Masculism has no doctrine on political violence; adherents are mainly concerned with violence against men in the home and in war.

war-builds-character.rationale: Farrell treats war as the clearest case of men being expendable and told it is glory, so he would deny it is good for a nation's character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Christian masculinist and secular strands differ, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian masculinist movements might say yes while the progressive strand would say no, so adherents split.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Masculists want to reform public family courts, not privatise courts, but take no stance on the principle.

military-superiority.rationale: Farrell's military concern is that only men are registered and killed, not how strong the armed forces should be, so this is left neutral.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Ethnic composition of the nation is unrelated to masculism and its adherents hold varied views.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Masculists frame history through sex roles, not class, and Farrell says neither sex held power in the past; inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Farrell attributes pay gaps to life choices rather than discrimination, implying equal outcomes are not a proper goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not among the issues listed for masculism in Farrell's work or the reference overview.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss colonial history or reparations between states.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political union by religion or civilization is not a topic in masculist writing.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Farrell argues men are taught self-sacrifice as protectors, yet he frames the fix as mutual interdependence ('when either sex wins, both lose') rather than an ethic of self-interest; no clear answer follows.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Farrell criticises the male duty to earn and to be drafted as an unequal obligation, which suggests wariness of duty-first rhetoric.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental ethics is not discussed in masculism; Farrell's whales-versus-males line is rhetoric, not a view on nature's worth.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy does not appear in masculist sources.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Masculists criticise the male role in industrial work and war, but no source passes judgement on industrial civilization as a whole.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Masculist writing does not take up the pace of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Enhancement technology is not a topic in Farrell or the masculism literature.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No masculist source discusses algorithms or AI in government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy and encryption are outside the masculist agenda as described in the sources.

restore-past-order.rationale: Traditionalist masculinism wants to restore a lost order, while the progressive strand rejects that.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Farrell relies on outcome data but masculism has no stated stance on pragmatic policy judgement.

direct-action.rationale: Masculist groups use lobbying, protest and conferences, but there is no stated rule against elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: The masculist movement campaigns through books, lawsuits and lobbying, but no source states a principle about matching methods to goals.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred from the movement's demands, which seek equal treatment for men in modern courts, schools and health systems rather than an exit from modern society; no source discusses foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Farrell sees the roles of earning and child rearing as traded off rather than abolished; he wants flexibility, not abolition, inferred.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Masculist authors do not discuss distribution principles; their claims concern sex-based unequal treatment.

production-for-use.rationale: The profit motive versus production for need is not discussed by masculist sources.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Farrell says men trade power and health for pay as a choice, not as exploitation by owners, but there is no stated view on profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Inferred from masculism's reliance on rights claims, courts and legislatures in liberal democracies; no masculist source discusses class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Agricultural organisation is absent from masculist writing.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Farrell condemns that men are the ones sent to die in war but does not trace war to capitalism or any economic system.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed by masculist sources, though some libertarian-leaning adherents say yes.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed in masculist sources; Farrell argues for equal accountability but not a general liberty principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Masculists claim men as a group are disadvantaged, which is a group-rights style claim, yet they stress equal treatment of individuals.

conscription.rationale: Masculist writers such as Farrell object to a draft that applies to men only; that is a claim about equal treatment, and they take no clear position on whether conscription itself is acceptable.

exit-over-voice.rationale: No masculist source compares emigration and voting as checks on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss models of government administration.

positive-liberty.rationale: Farrell defines power as control over one's own life, which is close to a positive-liberty idea, but he applies it to gender roles only and takes no position on material guarantees.

media-academia-power.rationale: Masculists complain that academia, schools and media favour women's issues, but whether these outweigh elected officials is not stated.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Race and genetics are not discussed in the masculism literature; Farrell uses race only as an analogy against a male-only draft.

organic-representation.rationale: Masculists organise through advocacy groups within party democracy and say nothing about corporatist or family-based representation.

total-state.rationale: Masculists oppose state-enforced gender roles and see family courts as overreaching, so a state directing all life is inferred to be rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: Davidson's virism blames decline in masculine values, but it is one thinker's view and not shared by the progressive strand.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Masculist sources take no position on territorial expansion; the only war-related theme is the male burden of fighting.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Inferred from masculism's framing as an equal-rights movement in modern states; feudal oaths of loyalty are never discussed.

bound-labor.rationale: Not part of masculism; inferred rejection from its concern about obligations forced on men.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Masculist scholarship claims gender studies reflect a female standpoint, but whether all knowledge is power-laden is not stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Masculism frames itself as advocating for one sex's interests, but has no stated view on a unitary common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Masculist sources do not address Zionism or Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship is not a masculist issue in any source.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is absent from the masculism literature.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporate governance and worker votes do not feature in masculist writing.

school-vouchers.rationale: Masculists favour boy-friendly schooling such as single-sex options, which fits choice, but there is no stated view on vouchers.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed by Farrell or the masculism sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: No masculist source links political and economic freedom; adherents span economic ideologies.

rule-by-example.rationale: The masculism literature does not discuss whether rulers should govern by moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Masculist writing does not address nationhood or self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Masculist sources raise war only to object that men bear its deaths; the legal authority for using force is not discussed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Mythopoetic and evangelical strands appeal to myth and faith while Farrell appeals to data, so adherents differ.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Who qualifies for welfare by citizenship is not addressed in masculist sources.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; Farrell's duty-to-earn critique cuts both ways.

class-collaboration.rationale: Farrell rejects a zero-sum struggle between the sexes, but neither he nor other masculists apply that to employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural institutions and futurist views of heritage are outside anything masculist sources discuss.

dominated-front.rationale: Anti-Western alliances between states are not a topic in masculist writing.

workers-nation.rationale: Masculist sources say nothing about organising the working class nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The progressive masculist strand seeks flexible roles for both sexes and calls male-only duties discrimination, while the traditionalist strand would agree; the documented mainstream disagrees.

ban-interest.rationale: Lending and interest are not discussed in masculism.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Incompatible with the movement's equal-treatment framing; inferred.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Masculists see the state as biased toward women in family law rather than as a ruling-class tool; inferred.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Fossil-fuel production is not a masculist issue in any source, though Farrell notes men do most mining and oil work as hazardous jobs.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss immigrant integration.

elite-replacement.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists claim elites favour women, a different claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not addressed by Farrell or the masculism literature.

national-mission.rationale: No masculist source speaks of a national mission to spread a form of government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Masculists deny that men as a group hold systematic power; Farrell calls male power largely a myth and masculist scholarship rejects universal patriarchy, though the male-supremacist strand sees male dominance as natural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Farrell argues that powerful-looking men are not truly powerful, but masculists do not make a general populist claim about corrupt elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Nothing in masculism supports coercive state control of reproduction, and masculists object to men lacking reproductive say; inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Accountability for past state killings is outside masculism and not discussed in its sources.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Masculists want the state to reform family law and courts, yet no source states how limited government should be.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No masculist source endorses it; equal-rights framing implies rejection.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The progressive strand frames its aim as ending discrimination against either sex, which implies equal rights before the law; the supremacist fringe would dissent.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Revolutionary strategy is entirely outside the masculism literature.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss settler colonialism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Not addressed; masculists favour sex-neutral family law, but the statement concerns religious personal laws.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Laws on religious conversion are not discussed by masculists, whose religious wing (such as South African evangelical men's groups) is about male roles, not conversion law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cattle slaughter laws have no connection to any masculist source.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Masculists discuss boys' disadvantage in schools, not religious instruction; the Christian evangelical and secular strands would likely differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Theories of the socialist state are absent from masculist writing.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Farrell ties rights to responsibilities (voting and draft registration), but no masculist source states a theory of political legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are not discussed in masculism.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from equal-treatment framing; no masculist source addresses it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Masculists condemn violence against men, but no source endorses the libertarian non-aggression principle as a general rule.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed; Farrell says 'when either sex wins, both lose', which cuts against zero-sum struggle in the gender field only.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Banning anti-constitutional parties is outside masculism and not discussed in its sources.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican theories of freedom are not discussed in masculist sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional checks and balances are not a masculist topic; the movement criticises family courts' rulings, not their place in the constitution.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist party organisation is foreign to masculist writing.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Farrell notes that men are most of the homeless, but masculists do not argue that institutions should prioritise the poor generally.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Social-housing tenure is not discussed by masculist sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strike law does not appear in the masculism literature.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss the causes of poverty or population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Ethnic diversity and social cohesion are not discussed in masculist writing.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials by lot is not a masculist topic.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Masculists complain about weakened due process for accused men, so they would resist suspending protections; inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Food price controls are not discussed by masculists.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not part of masculism; inferred from advocacy-based politics.

party-commands-army.rationale: Civil-military command structures are not discussed in masculism, beyond objection to male-only conscription.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not addressed in masculist sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Legislators' pay is not a masculist issue in any source.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Masculist sources do not discuss internal party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Supranational unions such as the EU are not discussed by masculists.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The division of executive and legislative powers is not addressed in masculist writing.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not discussed even by the evangelical masculinist groups described in the sources.

clerical-rule.rationale: Nothing in masculist sources supports rule by clergy, and the main strand is secular and egalitarian; inferred.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Not addressed, though Farrell criticises men being sent to die.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Masculists complain of misandrist media, but there is no endorsement of censorship; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Presidential term rules are outside anything masculists write about.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of elected officials is not a masculist topic.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Farrell objects to who is sent abroad to fight, not to alliances or overseas deployments as such, so no answer follows.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed in masculist sources.

people-in-arms.rationale: No masculist stance on replacing professional armies; only the male-only burden of service is addressed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Masculist writing does not compare rural and urban moral life; the mythopoetic strand's wilderness retreats are about male identity, not settlement.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Divided nations and reunification are not discussed by masculists.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists criticise gender-studies academics.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Masculist sources do not rank or compare cultures and civilizations.

death-penalty.rationale: Masculists complain that men receive harsher sentences, but there is no common view on capital punishment itself.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Masculists back gender equality teaching in principle but criticise school curricula as favouring girls, so adherents are split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science curricula are not discussed; masculists' school concerns are boys' falling achievement.

restrict-pornography.rationale: No settled masculist position; mythopoetic and Christian strands might favour limits while others value free expression.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Rules for acquiring citizenship are not addressed in masculist sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Minority language policy is not a masculist issue.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious exemptions from general law are not discussed in the masculism literature.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Farrell wants roles to loosen for both sexes, but this specific claim about conformity is not addressed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International debt relief is not discussed by masculists.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Decolonisation and economic transformation are outside masculist writing.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitutional rewriting is not a masculist topic.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Masculist sources do not weigh political freedom against development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid duties are not discussed by masculists.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not addressed in masculist sources.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How the head of state is chosen is not discussed in masculism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central bank governance is not a masculist topic.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial concessions for peace are not discussed in masculist writing.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The justification of private property is not discussed by masculists.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The nature of the Soviet economy is not discussed in masculist sources.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is not a masculist topic.

collective-defense.rationale: Mutual-defence alliances are not discussed; Farrell's war concern is the male-only draft.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation law are outside masculist writing.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: State control of clergy is not a masculist topic in any source.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a head of state is not discussed by masculists.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Masculist sources do not address secession or its suppression.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Autonomy arrangements for regions joining a state are not discussed by masculists.

sacred-ruler.rationale: No masculist source supports sacral rule and the movement is modern and egalitarian; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax structure is not discussed by masculist authors.

character-from-environment.rationale: Farrell attributes male behaviour largely to socialisation and father absence, an inference to the general claim.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Masculists press for equal treatment under law, so rulers above law is inferred to be rejected.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is not a masculist topic.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is absent from masculist writing.

leader-cult.rationale: Not part of masculism; inferred from its egalitarian mainstream.

equal-parenting.rationale: Farrell's central custody claim is that children do best with about equal time with each parent, and he wants courts to presume shared time.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Maoist theory of class struggle has no counterpart in masculist sources.

land-redistribution.rationale: Land reform is not discussed by masculists.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not addressed in masculist sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentist claims based on co-ethnics abroad are not a masculist topic.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Masculism's liberal strands favour individual freedom and no masculist source endorses punishing apostasy; inferred from general equal-rights framing.

women-must-cover.rationale: Masculists want sex-neutral law and flexible roles, so a rule imposing dress duties only on women is inferred to be rejected.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed by masculists.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-national unity of kin peoples is absent from masculist writing.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural autonomy is not discussed in masculist sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Masculists explain gender roles partly by past survival needs (men as protectors and providers), but no source takes a general position on historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed by masculist authors.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm bailouts are not a masculist topic.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Outside masculism, though masculists criticise family courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Farrell argues affirmative action increases inequality and that feminism favours women, so mandated equal representation of women is opposed as favouritism.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic colonial trade blocs are not discussed by masculists.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Labour and environmental clauses in trade deals are not discussed in masculist sources.

moral-incentives.rationale: Masculist writing does not take up work incentives under socialism.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Guerrilla theory is entirely outside masculism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Hereditary titles are not discussed by masculists.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History curricula are not addressed; masculist school concerns are about boys' achievement.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: No masculist source supports it; inferred from the equal-rights framing.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotic schooling is not discussed in masculist sources, though Farrell criticises slogans that teach boys duty to be drafted.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Farrell argues affirmative action increases inequality; extending that to race is an inference, not a documented masculist position.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not a masculist topic.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The resilience of capitalism is not discussed by masculists.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Post-imperial influence is not discussed in masculist sources.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory trade policy is outside masculist writing.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The theory of a labour aristocracy is not discussed by masculists.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Outside masculism; masculists oppose sex discrimination, so some would disagree.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not a masculist topic.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Farrell's gender-liberation approach frees men from rigid roles, which implies tolerance, though no direct statement was found.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Masculists oppose male-only conscription, but that is a demand for equal duty or abolition of the draft, not abolition of the armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Uneven development strategy is not discussed in masculist sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Masculists complain of media bias on gender, but no source addresses ownership by wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: masculist grievances about custody and conscription call for equal, rule-bound treatment rather than discretion.

racial-franchise.rationale: The progressive strand seeks equality for both sexes and has no racial exclusion; the scope excludes the male-supremacist strand.

online-participation.rationale: Online political deliberation is not discussed in masculist sources, despite the movement's later online presence.

open-government-data.rationale: Government transparency rules are not a masculist topic.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: the progressive strand stresses equal rights in marriage and family law, with no religious limits.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy and rent caps are not discussed in masculist sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: The order of cultural and state building is not a masculist topic.

god-not-male.rationale: The egalitarian strand has no stated view on religious language.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Redrawing regions along ethnic lines is not discussed by masculists.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not a masculist issue; adherents range across economic views.

municipal-property.rationale: Ownership of the means of production is outside masculist concerns.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The legal basis of regional self-government is not a masculist topic.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetically modified crops are not discussed by masculists.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density and the environment are not discussed in masculist sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret versus open diplomacy is not a masculist topic.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Exploitation of poorer regions within a state is not a masculist topic.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not a masculist issue and adherents range across economic views.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in masculist sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: No masculist source takes a side on targeted versus universal social spending.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Farrell's gender-liberation aim and equal parental rights imply either spouse may seek divorce; inferred, not stated.

notes: Strands differ: the progressive strand seeks equality for both sexes, the mythopoetic and Christian strands favour distinct gender roles, and the extremist strand promotes male supremacy. Wikipedia notes the term is also used for antifeminism and machismo.
